newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close firm as leaders echo bill gains.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close firm as leaders echo bill gains.

text.p: * Leaders firm slightly across the board as bill rates ease
* Offshore buyers dominate, locals' thoughts on rugby
* Fletcher Energy tops turnover, gains six cents
Price movements at the close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +7.33 at 2,492.30
136 nil * NZSE-10 cap index +6.33 at 1,256.80
376 +2 * NZSC cap index -10.82 at 5,238.75

758 +5 * Other movers - +6 -9
The New Zealand stock market closed firmer on Thursday as a partial reversal of recent bill market rate rises boosted leaders across the board.
The NZSE40 index ended the day 7.33 higher at 2,492.30 as 90-day interest rates fell 20 basis points to 8.34 percent in tandem with a rebound by the dollar's Trade Weighted Index.
Nigel Scott at brokers BZW said the highlight of good turnover of $73 million was Fletcher Energy which closed up six cents at NZ$4.93 with 4.26 million shares traded.
Richard Dwyer at brokers Hamilton Hindin Greene said the tone improved after opening marginally lower.
"It started off fairly slow actually and volume picked up as the day went on, apart from a few big crossings, including Fletcher Energy, early on," Dwyer said.

Scott said a rise in the kiwi dollar against the U.S. and Australian currencies, which helped the TWI accelerate to 64.76 from 64.36 yesterday, and a fall in interest rates contributed to a "pretty good performance" by the New Zealand market.
"Given several market participants have left for Melbourne (for the New Zealand-Australia Rugby Test match on Saturday) the market was probably dominated by offshore players today," Scott said.

He said a fall in the small companies index, which closed off 10.82 at 5,238.75, reflected the absence of local buyers as the rugby migrants and fears of higher mortgage interest rates took their toll.
Dwyer said investors were expecting further falls in wholesale interest rates and that had helped the mood.
